A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching models, prompting strategies and synthetic experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original anomaly-detection experiments across eight synthetic datasets, alongside model-validation and arithmetic-impairment experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds Yahoo S5 benchmark results and a human anomaly-detection validation study.

M1.justification: The prompting framework, textual and visual representations, 21 prompt variants, JSON interval outputs and synthetic-data generation algorithm remain unchanged. The added evaluations and mathematical descriptions do not establish a changed algorithm or model.

E1.justification: v3 extends anomaly-detection evaluation beyond the eight custom synthetic datasets to Yahoo S5, containing 67 real computational-service series and 300 synthetic series. Appendix B also introduces human detection validation, adding a population absent from v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within every retained experiment. Yahoo S5 uses the same four investigated LLMs, Isolation Forest and Thresholding already evaluated in v1; newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The retained synthetic protocols remain unchanged. Added protocols include Yahoo S5 evaluation with eight prompt variants per model on a corpus described as 367 series of length 1500, and a five-participant validation using 20 subtle anomalies with an obvious-anomaly comparison.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a small human study testing whether flat-trend anomalies are perceptually difficult; v1 asserted this difficulty without direct human validation. Existing CoT, noise, arithmetic-impairment, subsampling and representation analyses remain, including the model-family analysis relocated to Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The Isolation Forest random state remains 42. The added human study reports aggregate detection outcomes without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All 580 result rows in retained Tables 2–9 match exactly. New Table 10 adds 34 Yahoo S5 rows, including GPT-4o-Mini affinity F1 of 72.19 for zero-shot vision and 41.26 for subsampled zero-shot text. Human validation adds reported detection outcomes of 0/20 subtle versus 17.2/20 obvious anomalies, substantially extending the empirical evidence.

T1.justification: New Appendix E formalizes the existing repetition-bias and arithmetic hypotheses through definitions, accuracy inequalities and an optimal-detector assumption, without adding proofs. Section 3.1 also corrects anomaly membership from belonging to all anomalous intervals to belonging to any interval.

C1.justification: The abstract materially narrows the central conclusion: v1 states that LLMs can understand time-series anomalies, whereas v3 limits this to trivial anomalies and explicitly finds no evidence for understanding subtler real-world anomalies. The introduction consequently emphasizes caution, while retaining the principal mechanism-related findings.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explicit real-world applicability limitation and explains the choice of synthetic data through label quality, anomaly isolation and CoT-description requirements. It also explains why discrete interval outputs preclude VUS evaluation. Interpretations of the retained controlled experiments largely remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project repository link and reports availability of synthetic-data generators, final prompts and evaluation scripts. It also documents Yahoo S5 composition and its source. Existing deployment instructions, prompt examples, interpolation details and generator parameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Dong et al. (2024) when positioning visual reasoning, Laptev and Amizadeh for Yahoo S5, and Paparrizos et al. for VUS. The broader research positioning remains similar; numerous other reference changes update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: Parts of the introduction, related work and anomaly definitions are rewritten or clarified. Hypothesis 7 and its detailed discussion move to Appendix C, with a short model-variation discussion retained in the main text. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands dataset visualization through nine new multipanel figures, Figures 9–17, covering the eight synthetic datasets and Yahoo S5. It also adds Table 10, expands explanatory captions and rearranges several existing displays. Retained result tables preserve their structure and numerical content.

improvement.justification: Yahoo S5 evaluation and direct human validation strengthen evidence missing from v1, while narrower headline claims, dataset illustrations and code-access information improve calibration and usability. The gains remain limited: Yahoo results combine real and synthetic series, the five-person study is sparsely documented, and Appendix E introduces a problematic noise bound whose minimum separation is zero for periodic repetitions.
